title: I'm not a game dev. Two weeks with Meshy, Fable 5.2 and three.js and I have a horror game running in the browser
author: Reasonable_Use_8915
selftext:
I'm not a game dev. Mid November I started making a horror game alone with AI, and it actually runs in a browser and on your phone. It's called Shadewick, its free, no download no sign-up. You collect the pieces and don't look at what's following you.

The part I find interesting is how it get's made, so here it is.

Every 3D asset comes from Meshy. The monster, the survivors, every prop. 1. I start with a concept in ChatGPT, generate the model 
2. in Meshy and rig it there. 
3. But raw models are not game ready, not even close. So each one goes into Blender and I clean it up with Fable 5.2, which is also what I use for the code on top of three.js.

500+ generations so far. 

I burned through all my credits. Trust me, the real cost is not the tool, it's how many tries it takes to get one model that looks right and still runs in a browser.

The survivors or heros are voiced with ElevenLabs almost for free they offer 30k free a month

The lighting and reflections I built into the game "myself".

Use heavy on the three.js library and examples to get fluids and flames working

A few years ago someone like me couldn't have shipped anything at all. Now I'm asking a sub full of people who do this for real for notes, which is kind of wild to me.

So for those of you doing 3D with AI, how are you getting models game ready? Is cleanup in Blender the norm or is there a better pipeline I'm missing?

if you want to try it 
https://play.shadewick.com/
